item.title: 5 reasons to question ecology
item.description:
• Because the consumption of cereals and dairy products requires immense areas for cereal crops and pastures, which devastate the primitive forest and are now seriously damaging the planet.
  • Because direct contact with the flavors of food leads to discerning good from bad crops, and therefore to promoting organic and biodynamic cultivation, respectful of the environment.
  • Because the love of fruits and other natural products awakens the love for nature that lies dormant in every man, beyond the fascination of the artifices of culture.
  • Because the biochemical denaturation of food molecules by culinary preparations generates a molecular disorder whose consequences in terms of soil and water pollution could be more serious than one imagines, in particular at the level of viral and parasitic diseases in the whole biocenosis.
  • Because the health of the organism and the health of the environment are one and the same.

Example: the Tasadays, a tribe living in the Philippines as in the Stone Age, had been consuming palm heart for millennia. “Thanks” to the ethnologists who discovered them in the 1970s, they learned to cook this food, so that they could consume much larger rations. After a generation, they were obese, and their forests decimated …

item.title: An empirical yet verifiable basis
item.description: It may seem strange to consider a series of paranormal phenomena as a valid empirical basis for any theory whatsoever. Yet the discovery of the fundamental relationship between Eros and development of psychic abilities brings a double factual basis for the psychoanalytic edifice, with all the consequences this can have on the entire theory.

item.title: Human Sexuality
item.description: From an ecological perspective, it is the relationship of sexuality to the environment in all its forms. It is necessary to consider the quality of one’s social environment, the affinities felt for a particular individual (or “energetic” affinities), the partner’s behavior, the image of sexuality conveyed by culture and morality, the acceptance or rejection of the existence of a transcendent dimension, but also dietary factors and their physiological and psychological repercussions.

item.title: The Dietary Factor
item.description: Not long ago, the influence of food on the body was systematically denied, provided that a minimum number of calories was consumed. Today, we know that it plays a major role in many diseases. What is less well known is its influence on mental functioning.
